clue.text: Material left by a church

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Fabric has been bequeathed to a parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate openwork fabric, so it is a type of material.

clue.text: Man sits on magical phone box, one coming out in panto gear?

parts.note: Leo is a man's name

indicators.note: coming out says the letter for one leaves the time machine

parts.note: the Tardis is Doctor Who's time machine, disguised as a police phone box
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man sits on top of a magic phone box, and someone emerges dressed for pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: The magical phone box is the time machine of the British TV series Doctor Who. In a down answer 'sits on' means placed above; 'coming out' drops the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-fitting stretchy garments like these are worn by dancers and by many pantomime performers on stage.

clue.text: To south of Scottish island see part of church crumble

indicators.note: in a down answer, to the south of means placed below the island

parts.note: Coll is an island of the Inner Hebrides
the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: South of a Scottish isle, a visitor sees part of a church falling down.
explanation.walkthrough: COLL is a small island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides; 'To south of' puts APSE beneath it in the down entry. 'see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall in or give way, the same as crumbling.

clue.text: Seasonal food that comes with a sign of emotional stress?

definitions.meaning: the meat of a goose, a traditional Christmas roast
the bumpy skin raised by fear or strong feeling

explanation.surface: A festive dish arrives together with a symptom of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is the flesh of a goose, a classic festive roast; as one word it is the pimpled skin of fright or excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose meat is traditional winter holiday fare, and the bumps on skin appear when someone is frightened or moved.

clue.text: Once a tempestuous expanse of water

indicators.note: tempestuous means stormy, so the letters of once a are tossed about

explanation.surface: Once there was a stormy stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tempestuous' rearranges ONCE A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, the largest kind of sea.

clue.text: Brief statements from married stars putting tot to the fore

indicators.note: to the fore says the word for tot goes at the front

parts.note: to tot up is to sum, so a tot is a sum
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Short reports from celebrity couples, with a toddler pushed to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' is a noun in the surface (a toddler) but works as a sum, as in totting up a bill; 'to the fore' places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Summaries are short accounts giving the main points, so they are concise statements.

clue.text: Manage funds reallocated for recreational activities

indicators.note: reallocated means shared out again differently, so the letters of manage funds are rearranged

explanation.surface: Money is moved about to pay for leisure pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reallocated' rearranges MANAGE FUNDS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means playful amusement and merriment, light-hearted leisure and pastimes.

clue.text: Praises partner of yesteryear, sadly lost

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of lost are in a sorry jumbled state

explanation.surface: Someone speaks warmly of a former partner who has, unfortunately, passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' reads as bereavement but is the fodder that 'sadly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so extols means praises.

clue.text: Hurry to entertain artist turning up in African city

indicators.note: to entertain means to take in as a guest, so the hurry word holds the other

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, to hurry

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters for artist are read upwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Rushing to host a painter who has arrived in an African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: An artist in crosswords is often a Royal Academician; 'turning up' reads it upwards in this down answer, and 'to entertain' houses it in the word for hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe in southern Africa.

clue.text: Paintings in works defaced

indicators.note: with its face, the front letter, removed, the word for works loses its head

parts.note: toils means works hard, labours

explanation.surface: Artworks inside a factory have been vandalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils is a common short name for oil paintings, pictures done in oil paint.

clue.text: Traitor involved with men becomes killer

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of traitor are tangled up together with those of men

explanation.surface: A traitor who joins a gang becomes a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes the letters of TRAITOR and MEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminator is one who ends things, here an assassin, as in the film's robotic hitman.

clue.text: Boy overwhelmed by a noise in pantomime

indicators.note: overwhelmed suggests the boy is swamped, surrounded by the other letters

parts.note: din means a loud noise
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A child at a pantomime is swamped by the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' means the boy sits inside the other letters; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This tale of a lamp and genie is one of the best-loved British Christmas pantomimes, a comic family stage show.

clue.text: Face tackling minister, beginning to irritate in the role of boss

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the face word wraps round the others

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock, or slang for a face
a rector is a parish minister

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of irritate

explanation.surface: Someone confronts a clergyman, starting to annoy him, while acting as the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' is a clock face here; 'tackling' has it grip the minister and the first letter given by 'beginning to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Directorial describes what pertains to a director, a person in charge or boss of a film or organisation.

clue.text: Girl attending university having endless 6 — like a bit of a target?

definitions.text: like a bit of a target?

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, meaning frolics, is a lark

explanation.surface: A girl at college having unlimited fun wonders whether she is like part of a dartboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to 6 down, whose answer is a synonym for LARK; 'endless' trims it to LAR. 'attending' and 'having' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped, and a target is made of concentric rings, so one bit of it is ring-like.

clue.text: Infernal place, Herts town, in which to perform — it's off-putting

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the city of hell in Dante

indicators.note: in which says the word for perform goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: Hell, or a Hertfordshire town, as a place to stage a show: both put the performer off.
explanation.walkthrough: The infernal place is Dis of classical myth; Herts is Hertfordshire, an English county north of London. 'in which' sets the performing word inside the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distracting draws attention away, which is off-putting to someone trying to concentrate.

clue.text: What supplies support for bridge?

parts.note: bridge here is the card game, and the support is the furniture it is played on, not an engineering structure

explanation.surface: A question about what holds up a bridge, like a pier or girder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests a structure over a river, but it is the card game, played on a folding table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding table is used for playing card games such as bridge, holding up the cards.

clue.text: Man's man?

parts.note: Man here is the Isle of Man, so a man belonging to it is someone living on that isle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's man' sounds like a macho type, but Man is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; its resident is an inhabitant of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from the Isle of Man is an inhabitant of an island, a Manx resident.

clue.text: Plant fellows found submerged under cold nasty clay

indicators.note: in a down answer, submerged under places the fellows below the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of clay are in a bad, messed-up state

parts.note: men are fellows

explanation.surface: A plant and some men are found buried beneath cold, unpleasant clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the clay; 'submerged under' puts the fellows at the bottom of this down answer. 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamen is a flowering plant with swept-back petals, popular as a winter houseplant.

clue.text: Celebrating the season? Starchy miss is otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters of starchy miss are reordered

explanation.surface: Is the prim, stiff young woman joining in the festive spirit? No, she is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges STARCHY plus MISS; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmassy means full of festive cheer, in the spirit of the December holiday season.

clue.text: For now, Prime Minister must swallow rubbish meeting European

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so the prime minister letters enclose the rest

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: For the time being, the premier has to accept nonsense when meeting a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must swallow' has the Prime Minister's initials hold the rest; 'meeting' is a link joining the rubbish to the European.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, meaning for the time being, temporarily.

clue.text: Group in the auditorium stopped from playing?

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so this signals a word as it is heard

parts.note: a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A musical group in a concert hall prevented from performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the auditorium' signals a soundalike: BAND, spoken, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Banned means prohibited, so a player who is banned is stopped from taking part.

clue.text: Once again embrace silly pater outside party

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go around the word for party
silly suggests the letters of pater are scrambled foolishly

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A foolish father, standing outside a party, wants to hug again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes REAPT from the father, and 'outside' wraps that round the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To readopt is to take up or embrace a cause, idea or child a second time.

clue.text: Make painful sound about donkey in carol-singing

indicators.note: about means the wailing word goes round the donkey

parts.note: to wail is to make a cry of pain
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey braying painfully at the carol singers, as in a nativity scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make painful sound' is a verb phrase that reads as the definition but gives the outer letters; 'about' wraps them round the donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is the old custom of going from house to house singing and toasting at Christmas.

clue.text: Home Counties rule set up for whole country

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east, SE
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: The region around London lays down a rule for the entire nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties around London, in the south-east. 'set up' reads both pieces upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is a nation in its own right within the United Kingdom, a country entire.

clue.text: Bouncer at annual event in London SW?

definitions.text: Bouncer at annual event in London SW?

parts.words: Bouncer at annual event in London SW?
parts.note: the event is Wimbledon, in south-west London, where the bouncing object is what players hit, not a doorman

explanation.surface: A doorman working at a yearly event in south-west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' looks like a security guard, but it is a thing that bounces. The annual event is the Wimbledon tennis championships, held in London SW19.
explanation.definitionFit: The ball used at Wimbledon bounces on the grass courts every summer, a playful sense of bouncer.

clue.text: The damsel supplies this cheese

indicators.note: supplies says the words the damsel provide the letters, contained in them

explanation.surface: A young lady provides a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, often sold coated in red wax.

clue.text: Eldest maid travelling round Egypt etc

indicators.note: travelling round suggests the letters of eldest maid move about into new places

explanation.surface: The oldest servant is on a tour of Egypt and nearby lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling round' rearranges ELDEST MAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is one of the countries of the region spanning south-west Asia and north-east Africa, so 'Egypt etc' names the region by example.

clue.text: Loveless grumble coming from senior family member

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless says that letter goes

parts.note: to groan is to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: A grumble from an unloving elderly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' removes O (love, as zero in tennis scores) from GROAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran is short for grandmother, an older relative in the family.
